exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Planning a Trip to the Maya Ruins
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lily: Sam, our class is planning a trip to the Maya ruins next month. Are you coming?
Sam: Of course! I've been fascinated by the Maya since I was little.
Lily: Me too. I really want to see one of those huge stone pyramids.
Sam: I'm more interested in their calendar. They tracked the stars so carefully.
Lily: That's amazing. Our guide says the writing on the walls still can't be fully read.
Sam: I know. No one has worked out every sign yet. It's a real mystery.
Lily: Let's bring notebooks and write down whatever the guide tells us.
Sam: Good idea. I can't wait to set out!
exercises.translation_cn: Lily 说班级下月要去参观玛雅遗址,问 Sam 去不去;Sam 当然去,从小就着迷玛雅;Lily 最想看巨大的石头金字塔;Sam 更感兴趣他们的历法和观星;导游说墙上的文字至今无法完全读懂;两人决定带笔记本,记下导游讲的内容。

options: The Maya calendar and their study of the stars.

questions.stem: What does the guide say about the wall writing?
options: It still cannot be fully read.

questions.stem: What do they decide to bring?
options: Notebooks to write down what the guide says.

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 The Maya Calendar
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The Maya were remarkable watchers of the sky.
Using only their eyes, they followed the movements of the stars and planets.
From this knowledge they built a calendar of great accuracy.
It lost only a few seconds each year, which is amazing for ancient times.
They did all of this without any of the machines we use today.
exercises.translation_cn: 玛雅人是了不起的观天者;仅凭肉眼追踪星辰和行星的运动;由此建立了极为精确的历法;每年只差几秒,这在古代令人惊叹;而这一切都没有借助我们今天使用的任何机器。

questions.stem: What were the Maya remarkable at?
How did they follow the stars?
What did they build from this knowledge?
How accurate was the calendar?
options: It was wrong by a whole month.
It lost only a few seconds a year.

questions.stem: What did they manage without?

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Why Did the Cities Fall?
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Emma: Jack, our history question asks why the Maya cities were abandoned. Any ideas?
Jack: The book says there wasn't just one reason. Several causes worked together.
Emma: Right. As the population grew, they needed much more land for farming.
Jack: So they cut down a lot of the forest. That may have harmed the land.
Emma: And then there were the droughts. The rains failed for years.
Jack: With less rain, the crops failed and food ran short.
Emma: No wonder the people finally left their homes.
Jack: Whatever the exact cause, the great cities slowly fell into ruin.
exercises.translation_cn: Emma 和 Jack 讨论历史题:玛雅城市为何被弃;Jack 说书上讲并非单一原因,多个原因共同作用;人口增长需要更多农田;于是砍掉大量森林,可能损害了土地;接着又有连年干旱、雨水不至;雨水减少导致作物歉收、粮食短缺;人们最终离开家园;无论确切原因如何,伟大的城市慢慢沦为废墟。

questions.stem: What is the history question about?
options: Why the Maya cities were abandoned.

questions.stem: According to Jack, how many causes were there?
Why did the people need more land?
What happened when the rains failed?
options: Crops failed and food ran short.

questions.stem: What finally happened to the great cities?

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 How Little We Know the Sea
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Beneath the oceans lie about three million shipwrecks.
Each one shows people trying to reach the edges of their world.
Yet today we have better maps of the Moon than of our own sea bed.
Only now are we learning to deal with the cold, darkness and pressure of great depths.
Much of the deep ocean is still waiting to be explored.
exercises.translation_cn: 海洋之下约有三百万艘沉船;每一艘都展现着人类努力抵达世界边缘;然而今天我们对月球的地图比对自家海床的还要详尽;直到现在我们才开始学会应对深海的寒冷、黑暗与压力;深海的大部分仍在等待被探索。

questions.stem: About how many shipwrecks lie beneath the oceans?

options: People trying to reach the edges of their world.

questions.stem: What do we have better maps of than the sea bed?

options: The cold, darkness and pressure of the depths.

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Talking to an Explorer
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Host: Dr Reed, you've explored some of the wildest places on Earth. What drives you?
Dr Reed: Simple curiosity. I just can't stop wondering what lies beyond the next hill.
Host: But aren't you ever afraid of the unknown?
Dr Reed: Of course. The trick is to subdue that fear and keep going.
Host: Many people would rather steer clear of such danger.
Dr Reed: True. But I always think twice and study the risks before I set out.
Host: So courage isn't the same as rushing in blindly?
Dr Reed: Exactly. A wise explorer looks into things carefully first.
exercises.translation_cn: 主持人问 Reed 博士是什么驱使她探险;她说只是纯粹的好奇,总忍不住想知道下一座山后面有什么;主持人问她难道不怕未知;她说当然怕,关键是克制恐惧、继续前进;很多人宁愿避开这种危险;但她出发前总会三思并研究风险;主持人问勇气是否等同于盲目冲入;她说正是如此,明智的探险者会先仔细调查。

options: She subdues it and keeps going.

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 A Word on Curiosity
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Throughout history, curiosity has pushed humankind forward.
It led our ancestors to discover fire and to cross unknown seas.
When you face something strange, you do not always have to run away.
Take a careful look, think it over, and you may learn something new.
Whatever you discover, the courage to explore is always worth it.
exercises.translation_cn: 纵观历史,好奇心一直推动人类前进;它引领我们的祖先发现火、跨越未知的海洋;当你面对陌生事物时,不必总是逃开;仔细看一看、好好想一想,你也许会学到新东西;无论你发现什么,勇于探索永远值得。
